text: One dollar and eighty seven cents. <break time="0.8s" /> That was all the money. <break time="0.8s" /> Della had and sixty cents of it. <break time="0.8s" /> Was in pennies. <break time="0.8s" /> She had saved those pennies. <break time="0.8s" /> One or two at a time. <break time="0.8s" /> By bargaining. <break time="0.8s" /> With the grocer and the butcher. <break time="0.8s" /> Three times. <break time="0.8s" /> Della counted the money. <break time="0.8s" /> And three times. <break time="0.8s" /> It was one dollar and eighty seven cents. <break time="0.8s" /> And the next day. <break time="0.8s" /> Would be Christmas. <break time="0.8s" /> There was clearly nothing to do but flop down. <break time="0.8s" /> On the shabby little couch. <break time="0.8s" /> And cry. <break time="0.8s" /> So Della did it. <break time="0.8s" /> Life she thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Is made up of sobs, sniffles, and smiles. <break time="0.8s" /> With sniffles in the lead. <break time="0.8s" /> Della and her husband, Jim. <break time="0.8s" /> Lived in a small furnished flat. <break time="0.8s" /> That cost eight dollars a week. <break time="0.8s" /> Not long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim had earned thirty dollars a week. <break time="0.8s" /> But now. <break time="0.8s" /> His pay had fallen to twenty. <break time="0.8s" /> Still whenever Jim came home. <break time="0.8s" /> Della ran to him. <break time="0.8s" /> And hugged him warmly. <break time="0.8s" /> That was a happy thing. <break time="0.8s" /> To see.
